newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Issing - Buba on target with long-term M3.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Issing - Buba on target with long-term M3.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing on Monday said the Bundesbank is on target with its longer-term money supply goals.

In an interview with Reuters Financial Television, Issing said that although the Bundesbank had missed its money supply target in half the cases in recent years, in the longer-term the central bank was still on target.
"In the longer-term we are on target," he said, adding that M3, the Bundesbank's key policy instrument, was still a useful indicator.
Over an average three year period, M3 is running at an average 5.5 percent, he said.
Issing has said in the past that Germany will not reach its target of four to seven percent M3 growth in 1996, after M3 grew at an annualised rate of 8.4 percent in October.

Against the backdrop of Germany's demands that the future European Central Bank should adopt a money supply target, Issing said: "Of course it would have been better if we had met the target." But he added that Germany's EU partners understood the reasons the targets were missed.

However, because the deutschemark effectively only has two years more to live, Issing said: "The council will naturally have to take this into account," when it meets to formulate its next money supply target.
Issing did not comment on the Bundesbank's next M3 target.
The Bundesbank traditionally sets a one-year money supply target, but independent economists have urged the central bank to adopt a longer-term target, making it easier to meet its goals.
